title: Read every supplier's export, whatever its delimiter

blocks.text: The catalogue import reads exports from several suppliers. Each supplier has its own delimiter character and a fixed number of columns, and any column may be left empty. The import has been fine with the suppliers that use commas and semicolons. A new supplier's file was rejected line by line, and lines from the old ones whose last column is empty end up on the review list.
Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/DelimitedFile.java`: `fields(line)` returns the line's fields when it has exactly one per column, and nothing otherwise.
When you're done, every supplier's well-formed lines are read, whatever the delimiter, and only lines with the wrong number of fields are rejected. About three lines in total.

cases.says: lines separated by semicolons are read into one field per column
a line with fewer or more fields than columns is rejected and kept for review
an empty column between two others is read as an empty field
a supplier whose delimiter is a pipe is read like any other: the delimiter is taken literally
a line whose last columns are empty still has one field per column and is accepted

origin.section: split() Takes a Regex and Drops Trailing Empty Strings

concepts: split(regex) removes trailing empty strings and keeps the others; a negative limit keeps every field.
split() reads its argument as a regular expression, so a delimiter such as | or . must be quoted.
